changes.oldText: Remove the standard handoff rule and ask old clients to supply it through an undocumented header.
changes.newText: Older requests omit a custodian because the service supplies the documented handoff. Moving that default behind an undocumented header leaves those callers without the behavior they rely on.

changes.oldText: Send forfeit through the old response and assume older clients will ignore it.
changes.newText: Older clients reject values outside win, loss, and draw, so sending forfeit through their existing response breaks the closed value contract.

changes.oldText: Replace the result value with a provenance object and make old clients parse it.
changes.newText: Existing clients read the result value as before; replacing it with an object changes the response shape they consume.

changes.oldText: Add retryable to the old response and assume older clients will treat it as nonterminal.
changes.newText: Version 1 clients treat an unknown state as terminal, so they will not treat this new value as retryable.

changes.oldText: Change InvoiceId on each reissue and make old clients discover the replacement by searching.
changes.newText: InvoiceId names the customer obligation. Changing it for each issue attempt breaks references that older clients use for that same obligation.

changes.oldText: Change the meaning of revoked to include pending without informing current clients.
changes.newText: Pending revocation is not final revocation. Folding it into “revoked” makes older clients interpret an unfinished state as the completed one.

changes.oldText: Return revocation-pending through the old state field and hope clients fail closed.
changes.newText: Older clients reject states beyond active and revoked, so revocation-pending cannot safely travel through their existing state field.

changes.oldText: Replace accepted/rejected with the reason text and require old clients to parse it.
changes.newText: Existing clients consume accepted or rejected. Replacing that status with free-form reason text removes the signal their response handling expects.

changes.oldText: Create a separate catalog for retired lessons and remove their stable IDs from the current one.
changes.newText: Progress records keep the retired lesson IDs. Removing those IDs from the catalog leaves existing progress references unresolved.

changes.oldText: Change the default list to include retired lessons and ask old clients to filter them.
changes.newText: Older clients expect the default result to contain active lessons only; they are not required to filter retired items out themselves.

changes.oldText: Make the revision field mandatory in old requests and reject existing calls.
changes.newText: Existing clients do not send this new request field. Requiring it rejects their current calls before the snapshot can be returned.

changes.oldText: Replace the edit-history field with a revision token and make old clients reconstruct edits.
changes.newText: Older clients read the edit history. Replacing it with a revision token removes information those clients still consume.

changes.oldText: Change the meaning of false to mean only that a message is available.
changes.newText: False currently means the publication did not occur. Reusing it to mean only that messages exist makes the established boolean misleading.

changes.oldText: Replace the boolean with a string message and expect old clients to parse it.
changes.newText: Older clients expect a boolean publication result; a string is a different response type they cannot consume as that signal.

changes.oldText: Replace the source request ID with each portion ID so old clients can address the latest split.
changes.newText: The original request ID carries the existing delivery promise. Replacing it with a vendor-portion ID loses that stable reference for older clients.

changes.oldText: Return only vendor portion IDs and remove the original request reference.
changes.newText: Returning only portion IDs removes the original request reference, so older clients cannot associate the split with the request whose delivery promise they track.

changes.oldText: Change the result to “draw” and keep the timeout reason only in a private log.
changes.newText: The public result still needs to distinguish timeout from withdrawal. Keeping the reason private while reporting draw hides that required distinction from result consumers.

changes.oldText: Store the input and code references only in a private process log that readers cannot access.
changes.newText: Reviewers need these references to inspect provenance. A process log they cannot access does not let them identify the data and code used for the published result.

changes.oldText: Resolve provenance from the latest dataset and code when the result is opened.
changes.newText: The latest dataset or code may differ from the versions that produced this result. Looking them up later can attach incorrect provenance.

changes.oldText: Log the entire address and package record whenever a label is printed.
changes.newText: The case excludes the complete address from general diagnostics. Logging the address and package exposes private shipment data beyond what explains the printed label.

changes.oldText: Use the latest sensor revision when displaying a prior calibration.
changes.newText: The replacement sensor may have a different revision or unit. Pairing an earlier offset with the latest sensor can make the old calibration readings incorrect.

changes.oldText: Reuse yesterday’s quotes even though the current request requires fresh prices.
changes.newText: Yesterday’s quote may reduce calls, but it misses the unchanged fresh-price deadline for this request.

changes.oldText: Sample failures while keeping all redundant success traces.
changes.newText: Sampling omits some failed runs even though the audit contract requires every failure; retaining redundant success traces does not repair that gap.

changes.oldText: Delete failure records first because they are less frequent than successful rows.
changes.newText: The audit requires every failed run, regardless of frequency. Deleting those records breaks that requirement.

changes.oldText: Persist one checksum globally without binding it to the revision ID.
changes.newText: Without binding the stored checksum to the revision ID, a later revision can reuse a digest for different bytes.
